completion_data.completion_summary: Broadened anti-analysis.md into a domain-agnostic 5-condition strategic-sorry acceptance test permitting main-target-level placeholders at deliberate skeleton division points; added a skeleton boolean and extended 7-field sorry_inventory schema to wrap-up.md with a --hard-only build-green exception (no 4th status enum value); updated skill-implementer-hard Stage 6 parsing/logging and general-implementation-hard-agent Stage 5 with an 'implemented (skeleton)' handoff example across both deployed and extensions/core dual copies (verified byte-identical); recorded an explicit downstream note that lean/cslib hard-mode overrides contradict the new core policy, flagged for a follow-up task via 772.

memory_candidates.content: Hard-mode contracts (.claude/context/contracts/anti-analysis.md, wrap-up.md) are single-copy files loaded exclusively by -hard skills/agents, so a policy relaxation confined to these two files is structurally --hard-only by construction; make that gate explicit with a one-line '--hard-only' note at the top of each contract so the invariant is stated, not just implied. When adding a new outcome type to a status-gated schema (e.g. an 'implemented (skeleton)' outcome), prefer adding a new boolean field alongside the existing status enum rather than a 4th enum value -- this avoids touching every status == "implemented" consumer (validate-handoff.sh, postflight gates) while still making the new outcome machine-distinguishable.

When editing dual-tracked skill/agent files (deployed .claude/skills|agents/ copy + .claude/extensions/core/ source copy) in this repo, diff the pair BEFORE editing -- pre-existing unrelated divergences (e.g. from other concurrently-landed tasks) are common and must not be conflated with divergence introduced by your own edit. Scope the post-edit diff check to 'no NEW differences beyond the pre-existing baseline' rather than assuming byte-identity was true before you started.
